title: Stall-hunt EOD log — short probes and todo
content:
EOD STALL-HUNT NOTES — Hiro Tanaka
Date: 2026-03-12 (ran through late afternoon probe)

Context:
- Intermittent ~200–800ms stall observed on streaming token generation for long-context requests (>4k tokens) on prod-dedicated-gpu-pool-03. Not consistent across requests; looks bursty (~3–4 events/hr).
- Customer impact: a few chat sessions saw stalled streaming which client retried and duplicated reply fragments. Need to find root (kernel/codepath/hardware).

Observed behavior (quick):
- P99 for token emit loop jumps from 45ms -> 680ms for single token emission under specific requests.
- Each stall corresponds to a gap in server stdout where the agent returns nothing for ~0.7s then resumes.
- No immediate full OOMs or process crashes.

Timeline (what I saw):
- 10:33: deploy of small perf patch (batcher tweak) to canary (PR 2147) — unrelated?
- 13:12: first customer report, trace id=trc_9f7a
- 13:18–13:40: reproduced on dedicated-03 by replaying noisy conversation (long prefix + few followups)
- 15:02: capture logs + run perf record (light) on runtime-worker-21
- 16:05: tried disabling prefix-KV cache on canary, stall still reproducible
- 16:50: grabbed nvtop snapshots; GPU util steady ~66% during stall windows

Quick checks performed:
- system: dmesg — no kernel OOM, no dmesg hangs indicated
- nvidia-smi pmon / nvtop — no sudden cooling/freq drops when stalled
- strace on worker during repro: saw futex->nanosleep loops (~700ms) then resumed
- perf record (100ms): user-space heavy on attention kernel during normal ops; during stall there was a thread blocked in pthread_cond_timedwait
- checked ulimits, no fd exhaustion

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) User-space condition variable timeout due to ordering bug in kv-cache invalidation (race where cache refill background thread signals incorrectly).
2) Batcher coalescing waiting longer because batcher not seeing new inbound requests — but network metrics show requests arriving at normal rate (reject hypothesis lower).
3) Kernel-level scheduling quirk on that instance due to a noisy neighbor process (less likely: isolated dedicated pool).
4) GPU-side synchronization (cuda stream wait) occasionally blocking host thread while waiting for small kernel to complete — nvprof didn't show long kernel times though.

Experiments run (notes):
- Experiment A: force synchronous flush on KV cache wake path (local debug build) — reduced frequency but not eliminated.
- Experiment B: run same replay with FORCE_SINGLE_THREAD=1 (disables concurrent refill) — stalls gone for 30m. Strong indicator race in concurrent refill/wakeup.
- Experiment C: increased batcher max-wait from 5ms -> 20ms to see if this coalescing changes pattern — no, stalls unchanged (so not batcher backoff).

Micro-trace (example):
[13:25:07.102] req=trc_9f7a token_emit start
[13:25:07.230] req=trc_9f7a token_emit blocked (pthread_cond_timedwait)
[13:25:07.948] req=trc_9f7a token_emit resume -> emitted token #142 (delta 718ms)

Immediate mitigation (for prod):
- Hotfix: set KV_CACHE_REFILL_CONCURRENCY=1 on dedicated-03 (rollout to 3 workers, monitor 2h). This is low-risk; limits parallelism but reduces concurrency surface.
- If hotfix reduces incidents, schedule proper fix. If not, rollback and gather more traces.

TODO (next, ordered):
- [ ] Add logging around cache->refill thread notify path (log timestamps + thread-id + seq) — quick PR, keep behind debug flag.
- [ ] Reproduce in local with stress harness (long prefix,+multi-concurrent replays) and run ASan build to catch race if present.
- [ ] Add per-thread timeline trace (micro-profile) emitting condvar/signal events to distributed tracing (open-telemetry) for 24h on canary.
- [ ] Run targeted perf (call-graph) during repro when concurrency=2 vs 1 and diff stacks.
- [ ] Add unit test to cache wake/sleep ordering (simulate background refill races) — aim for transient flakiness test.
- [ ] Postmortem skeleton (if fix lands) with customer timeline + mitigations.

Notes to self (quick):
- Remember to push logs to S3 for long retention (we lost some traces due to rotation at 48h).
- Ping @Maya Li about adding a small latency gauge on condvar-wait time in the console (per-route).
- If we flip concurrency to 1 as hotfix, annotate cost/perf impact in the rollout doc (throughput drop expected ~5–10%).

Questions for tomorrow pairing with Ethan:
- What is the intended ordering/handshake of refill->signal in cache design doc? (I recall an old caveat re: spurious wakeups but not this magnitude)
- Can we simulate with valgrind helgrind or tsan for our refill worker?

Scratch commands ran (notes):
- ssh runtime-21 -> sudo perf record -F 200 -p $(pidof runtime) -g -- sleep 20
- strace -f -tt -p <pid> > /tmp/strace.out & (filtered afterwards for futex/cond)
- GDB attach -> bt threads when stuck (saw pthread_cond_timedwait on thread 17)

Final quick thought:
- Strong signal that concurrency in KV refill/wakeup path has bad ordering; canary/1-thread experiment reduced incidence. Prioritize small fix (serialize notify or add explicit memory barrier/flushing) and add observability.

— Hiro
